facts: The Judgment was delivered by : Altamas Kabir, J.

Writ Petition (Civil) No.532 of 2008 was filed by Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam and Colonel Edwin Jesudoss (Retd.), challenging the Constitutional validity of the amendment of the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968
The same was taken up for final hearing along with several other Writ Petitions on account of the common issue involved therein.

The grievance of the Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam is that it had been refused recognition as a State party by the Election Commission of India, although, it secured 8.33% of the valid votes in the Assembly elections.

It is the further grievance of the Petitioners that in view of the amendment made to Cl. 6 of the Election Symbols Order, 1968, it had been denied recognition on account of the cumulative effect of the requirement that a political party would not only have to secure not less than 6% of the total valid votes polled, but it had also to return at least 2 members to the Legislative Assembly of the State.

It is the Petitioners' case that despite having secured a larger percentage of the votes than was required, it was denied recognition, since it had failed to return 2 members to the Legislative Assembly.
issues: The Constitutional validity of the amendment of the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968

The requirement that a political party would not only have to secure not less than 6% of the total valid votes polled, but it had also to return at least 2 members to the Legislative Assembly of the State.

Whether the Election Commission could have vested itself with the powers contained in Cl. 15 thereof, reserving to itself powers to settle issues in relation to splinter groups or rival sections of recognized political party, each of whom claimed to be the original party.
petitioner_arguments: The Petitioners' case that despite having secured a larger percentage of the votes than was required, it was denied recognition, since it had failed to return 2 members to the Legislative Assembly.

It is the further grievance of the Petitioners that in view of the amendment made to Cl. 6 of the Election Symbols Order, 1968, it had been denied recognition on account of the cumulative effect of the requirement that a political party would not only have to secure not less than 6% of the total valid votes polled, but it had also to return at least 2 members to the Legislative Assembly of the State.
respondent_arguments: The Election Commission's view that the provisions relating to recognition of political parties and their functioning, was required to be codified and provision was also required to be made for registration of political parties as a pre-condition for recognition.
The Election Commission's decision to streamline the provisions and procedure so long followed relating to recognition of political parties in the conduct of elections.
court_reasoning: This Court took note of the fact that the Election Commission had been clothed with plenary powers by Rules 5 and 10 of the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961, in the matter of allotment of Symbols, the validity whereof had not been challenged.

It was emphasized that there are certain authorities or persons who may be the source of rules of conduct and who at the same time could not be equated with authorities or persons who are entitled to make law in the strict sense.
holding: The amendment made to Cl. 6 of the Election Symbols Order, 1968, was held to be constitutional.

The requirement that a political party would not only have to secure not less than 6% of the total valid votes polled, but it had also to return at least 2 members to the Legislative Assembly of the State, was upheld.
